newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico first half May CPI rises 0.48 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexico first half May CPI rises 0.48 percent.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 0.48 percent in the first two weeks of May compared to the last two weeks of the previous month, Banco de Mexico said on Thursday.
A survey of 11 brokerages and research firms in Mexico City by Reuters found average expectations of a rise of 0.53 percent of the first two weeks.
The central bank said this was the smallest increase seen in the first half of a month in the last 29 months, since December 1994.
It said the main causes of inflation were increases in local telephone service, domestic gas, detergents, restaurants, some meats, and other products.
The increases were offset by a decline costs for domestic electricity use.
The central bank said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 0.43 percent in the first half of the month.
